plan:
FINAL EXPERIMENT DESIGN (design-only; nothing has been run and no outcomes are reported).

# 1. Question and claim structure
Primary question as asked: how do GPT-2 (124M) and CodeLlama-7B compare on RepoBench-P Python 'cross_file_first' completion, as deployed capability → answered by the NATIVE-context arm. Mechanism question (how much of any gap is "context starvation" vs model quality) → answered by the SHARED-1024-budget arm plus the truncated-vs-untruncated decomposition. Framing (per ruling Q2): an explicitly "general-purpose small vs code-specialized mid-size" capability contrast; a parameter-matched comparison is impossible (no 7B GPT-2, no 124M CodeLlama) and is a stated limitation, not adjusted away.

# 2. Data provenance and unit of evaluation
- Dataset: RepoBench-P v1.1, Python, cross-file setting with FIRST-DEPENDENCY prompts ("cross_file_first"), downloaded from the official RepoBench release (github.com/microsoft/RepoBench + HF). Official pre-built prompt files are used UNMODIFIED; no re-implemented dependency selection or retrieval. Retrieval quality is explicitly OUT of the comparison (scope boundary, per Q5).
- Split variant: primary = 'full' prompt variant (unmodified repository file contents), declared in advance, chosen because it is the faithful deployed condition and avoids a preprocessing step that could interact differently with the two models. The 'clean' variant is a pre-declared robustness replication (headline tables re-run on 'clean'; no cherry-picking — both reported). Exact cleaning semantics to be confirmed against the release README at data-staging time (data absent here).
- Unit: one completion instance per target file/line position as shipped: prompt = first-dependency file content + target-file prefix; reference = the following line(s) of the target file. Test set ≈1.7k line-level Python instances (design-time figure from the dataset card; exact count read from the staged split's metadata and recorded before any comparison).
- Instance alignment: both models evaluate the identical instance-ID list derived from the identical source prompt file. Rendered token sequences necessarily differ by tokenizer, but source text, ordering, IDs, and post-processing are identical.

# 3. Models and arms (per Q4 ruling)
| Arm | Model (HF checkpoint) | Role | Context budget | Data |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | openai-community/gpt2 (124M base) | Primary "small general" | native 1024 (GPT-2 BPE) | full test set |
| B1 | codellama/CodeLlama-7b-hf (base) | Primary "code mid-size" | native, capped at 8,192 tokens (declared) | full test set |
| B2 | CodeLlama-7b-hf | Shared-budget mechanism arm | 1,024 tokens (GPT-2-native-equivalent) | full test set |
| A2 | openai-community/gpt2-large (774M) | Bounded within-family scaling sensitivity | native 1024 | stratified subsample n=400 (rule in §6) |
| B3 | codellama/CodeLlama-7b-Instruct | Separated secondary arm | 8,192 cap | full test set; NEVER pooled with base arms |
Notes: (i) A1 doubles as the shared-budget GPT-2 run (native = 1024), stated openly; B2 is the budget-constrained CodeLlama. (ii) The 8,192 cap on B1/B3 is declared to bound prefill cost; the share of CodeLlama prompts exceeding 8,192 tokens is logged, and the cap is re-measured as a sensitivity if >20% of prompts are capped. (iii) Prompt format for B3: official Llama-2/CodeLlama chat template ([INST] with the RepoBench prompt verbatim as the user turn); base arms use raw continuation. Because prompt rendering differs, B3 is descriptive-only relative to A1/B1 and excluded from all paired confirmatory tests. (iv) CodeLlama-7b-Python is named as a design alternative NOT taken (one extra code-specialized variant is enough scope creep). (v) Precision fixed at bf16 for all arms, logged as a constant; quantization is dropped as an arm — under greedy decoding, modest quantization perturbs argmax ties only marginally and identically-in-kind across models, and it is a deployment rather than capability factor.

# 4. Decoding and post-processing protocol (fixed across arms)
- Decoding: greedy (do_sample=False, num_beams=1), max_new_tokens=64, no repetition/frequency penalty, no prefix caching differences (batched generation with per-sequence left padding; padding tokens masked).
- Truncation rule (declared): the target-file prefix (generation point) is ALWAYS preserved in full; if over budget, the first-dependency context portion is truncated from its interior, keeping the head (first k tokens) of the dependency file. Truncation event per (instance, arm) is logged as a boolean flag — this flag powers the §6 decomposition.
- Post-processing (RepoBench convention, identical for all arms): split generation to lines; keep line 1; keep subsequent lines only while they start with a whitespace character; stop at the first line whose first character is non-whitespace (dedent-to-column-0 cut); strip trailing whitespace. No model-specific post-processing.
- Determinism: greedy decoding, fixed model versions (git revisions recorded), single pass per instance. Generation failures: one retry in fp32; persistent failures marked "unavailable" with reason — never silently dropped (§6 missing-data rule).

# 5. Metric definitions (re-implementable)
Let p = post-processed model completion, r = reference completion (same line-keeping cut applied to nothing but the model output; references used as shipped), with per-line and whole-string comparisons on Unicode code points.
1. Exact Match (primary): EM(instance)=1 iff the line-sequence [l.strip() for l in p.splitlines()] equals that of r after stripping per line and after dropping trailing empty lines on both sides. Leading-indentation content is preserved up to strip() — i.e., EM is indentation-insensitive per line, matching the official RepoBench evaluation code, which strips before comparing (this convention is pinned by reading the official eval script at staging and recording it in the run manifest; if the official code compares without strip, that variant is adopted instead and noted).
2. Edit Similarity (co-primary): ES = 1 − Levenshtein(p′, r′) / max(len(p′), len(r′)), where p′, r′ are the stripped, newline-joined cleaned strings; convention: both empty → 1; exactly one empty → 0. Reported as instance-mean with CI.
3. CodeBLEU (tertiary only): the 'codebleu' PyPI implementation (Ren et al. 2020) with its Python tokenizer, corpus-level; fallback sacrebleu corpus BLEU with character tokenization and exponential smoothing if codebleu is unavailable on the execution stack. Reported with the standing caveat that corpus BLEU on ≤2-line completions is high-variance and n-gram-saturated; it is never used for claims or tests.
4. Cost metrics (§8): wall-clock per instance (prefill vs decode split), generated tokens, peak memory, per-instance FLOP estimate, EM-per-10^15-FLOPs.

# 6. Pre-registered analysis plan (all thresholds, families, and seeds fixed before any evaluation)
- Confirmatory family F1 (Holm–Bonferroni across exactly these four tests, α=0.05): (1) EM A1 vs B1, (2) ES A1 vs B1, (3) EM A1 vs B2, (4) ES A1 vs B2. EM differences tested with McNemar's test using the exact binomial test on discordant pairs over the intersected instance set; ES differences tested with the paired bootstrap below (no ad-hoc t-tests).
- Bootstrap: nonparametric instance-level resampling, B=10,000, percentile 95% CIs, seed 20261023 (single seed, fixed).
- Missing-data rule: primary analyses on the intersection of evaluable instances; counts and reasons per model reported; sensitivity analysis marks all unavailable instances as EM=0, ES=0 ("failure-as-wrong"); conclusions must agree across both views or be reported as divergent.
- Stratifications (descriptive unless named below): prompt-length buckets on a model-agnostic proxy — prompt character count thresholds {<1,200; 1,200–4,000; >4,000} chars (≈300/1,000 tokens); plus per-model truncation-flag decomposition (truncated vs not) applied to A1, B1, B2 — this is the declared mechanism analysis separating "worse model" from "context-starved model" (e.g., B1-vs-B2 gap within the untruncated stratum estimates pure-budget effect at matched content; within truncated instances, compare like-for-like where both were truncated). Repository-size and prompt-length strata beyond the named three are labeled exploratory/unadjusted. To prevent stratum fishing: only the three char-length buckets × EM for A1-vs-B1 receive Holm-adjusted "secondary confirmatory" status; all other cuts carry the label "exploratory, unadjusted for multiplicity."
- GPT-2-large subsampling rule (declared in advance): proportional stratified random sample, n=400, from the three char-length buckets, seed 20261023; reported descriptively as a within-family scaling sensitivity only; not pooled with A1.

# 7. Controls / factors held constant
Identical: instance set and order, source prompt text, dedent post-processing, max_new_tokens=64, greedy decoding, bf16, single reference per instance, same eval script for both models, same hardware class per pass (logged), fixed seeds for all resampling/subsampling. Intentionally varied: model checkpoint and its native tokenizer; context budget (the point of the arms); prompt rendering for B3 only (which is why B3 is descriptive-only).

# 8. Compute/efficiency section (in-body, per Q3)
Reported per arm: wall-clock per instance split into prefill/decode, total generated tokens, peak memory, per-instance FLOP estimate ≈ 2·P·(prompt+gen tokens) (forward-pass approximation, formula declared), and EM per 10^15 FLOPs. Design-time tractability estimate for the FULL ≈1,712-instance Python cross_file_first set: GPT-2 (≤1,088 tok): ≈2.7×10^11 FLOPs/instance → ≈5×10^14 FLOPs total — minutes-to-an-hour class on CPU/GPU. CodeLlama-7B at mean context ~3k (cap 8,192): ≈4×10^13 FLOPs/instance → ≈10^17 FLOPs total; on an A100-40/80GB (bf16, effective 50–150 TFLOP/s) roughly 1–8 h per full-set pass including decode-bound overhead (110k generated tokens/instance-set); CPU-only would be days — infeasible in practice. B2 (1,024-token cap) costs ~3–8× less per prefill than B1; B3 adds roughly one more full CodeLlama pass; A2 (n=400, 774M) is negligible. Full iso-FLOP / compute-matched curves are OUT of scope by ruling and appear in limitations.

# 9. Feasibility (per Q6)
(a) This container cannot execute the design: Python 3.14.4 with no torch/transformers wheels available, no ML stack at all (numpy absent), RepoBench data and both checkpoints absent, network disabled (DNS failures verified), CPU-only (no /dev/nvidia*). (b) Minimum execution environment: Python 3.10–3.12; torch ≥2.1 + transformers + the official RepoBench eval utilities; network or pre-staged artifacts (RepoBench-P v1.1 Python cross_file_first files; gpt2, gpt2-large, CodeLlama-7b-hf, CodeLlama-7b-Instruct); one GPU with ≥24 GB VRAM (7B bf16 ≈ 13.5 GB weights + KV cache ≈ 4 GB at 8,192 tokens ≈ 18 GB total; 40 GB comfortable). (c) Honest cost: §8 — full-set CodeLlama pass ≈ 1–8 GPU-hours, GPT-2 passes negligible; total all-arms run is single-digit GPU-days worst case, i.e., tractable for a real study but not in this container. No pilot is planned, claimed, or projected.

# 10. Limitations and threats to validity
1. Context asymmetry: native arm rewards CodeLlama's 32k window by design; the shared-budget arm bounds but does not eliminate the confound (tokenizer efficiency still differs at 1,024 tokens — GPT-2 BPE vs Llama SentencePiece pack the same prompt into different token counts, so "1,024 tokens" is not "1,024 tokens of content").
2. Tokenizer/vocabulary effects: EM operates on decoded strings, but indentation is whitespace-critical in Python; BPE 'Ġ'-merge vs SentencePiece whitespace handling and the dedent-stop rule can truncate the noisier 124M model's generations earlier than CodeLlama's — a scoring-path asymmetry mitigated only by the shared post-processing rule.
3. Not scale-matched: base-vs-base compares 124M general vs 7B code-specialized; the study cannot attribute the gap to code specialization vs scale (A2 offers only a weak within-GPT-2 direction check).
4. Single dataset/language: RepoBench-P Python only; generalization to other RepoBench languages, other units (cross_file_concat, intra_file), or other benchmarks is not covered.
5. Greedy decoding at 64 tokens is a known degeneration regime for a 124M model (repetition loops); EM/edit-similarity under greedy may understate GPT-2's sampling-quality capability. Held fixed for symmetry; flagged, not corrected.
6. Pretraining-contamination asymmetry: CodeLlama's GitHub-heavy pretraining may include RepoBench's repos, inflating verbatim recall; diagnostic (not corrective): report the rate of completions that match the reference verbatim beyond what prefix continuation predicts. Full mitigation impossible without held-out repo splits.
7. Prompt-quality noise: official prompts can contain near-leaks of the reference (dependency file containing the target line); spot-checked and reported as an overlap rate, since using prompts unmodified is a requirement.
8. The 8,192 cap on B1/B3 truncates a logged minority of prompts; if >20% capped, a 32k sensitivity is promised in advance.
9. 'full'-vs-'clean' choice: replication addresses it, but the primary is pre-committed either way.

# 11. Rationale — what each choice excludes
Official pre-built prompts → excludes retrieval-pipeline confounds. Native-window primary → excludes an artificial handicap on the 32k model for the deployed-capability claim; shared-1024 first-class arm → excludes "model vs context" conflation, the only design that does. Base-only primary → excludes prompt-format confounds (Instruct quarantined, never pooled). Greedy + fixed 64 tokens + shared dedent cut → excludes decoding/search asymmetry as an explanation. Paired McNemar + fixed-seed bootstrap + pre-declared Holm family → excludes analytic flexibility/fishing. Failure-as-wrong sensitivity + reported counts → excludes survivorship bias from silent drops. Full-test-set primary with one pre-declared subsample rule (A2) → excludes convenient subsampling. Required in-body cost table without iso-FLOP matching → answers "how does performance compare" without silently converting to a compute-efficiency study.

context.question: How does the performance of a small language model (e.g., GPT-2) compare to a larger code-specialized model (e.g., CodeLlama-7b) on the RepoBench Python dataset for the 'cross_file_first' setting?
context.context: Design an experiment that answers the question. The researcher can clarify source-supported setup details by topic. Do not claim that an experiment was run.
